correctness.rationale: The known homeomorphism with the tangent sphere bundle of a sphere gives the complete rational Betti degrees by the Gysin sequence and proves orientability. The published one-reflection action determines every dihedral character because rotations of order five act trivially on one-dimensional rational lines. A transposition of colors fixes a maximal cell and reverses two simplex factors, hence preserves the global orientation. The natural projection to the simplex boundary induces an isomorphism on rational cohomology in the middle base degree for odd n by the regular-neighborhood construction and Euler-class-zero Gysin sequence, proving the sign character of color relabeling. Poincare duality gives the complementary sign, and finite-group rational transfer gives the quotient. The standalone exact signed-Lefschetz enumeration agrees for 4,5,6 colors (15 generator tests), including the mixed n=5 trace four. The computation is only corroboration, not infinite-size proof.

originality.rationale: Kozlov 2005 gives nonequivariant integral cohomology, Schultz 2005 gives the Stiefel identification and one-reflection homotopy-equivariant model, and the 2014 article gives the one-reflection homeomorphism, explicitly leaving full dihedral homeomorphism equivariance open. These do not state the full simultaneous D5-by-color-S_n homology character or the all-n parity of the quotient by both groups. Two known isolated dihedral-only quotient calculations at n=4 and n=5 give no color-label representation. The argument genuinely establishes the missing target-sign and top-orientation behavior rather than treating the Stiefel homeomorphism as fully jointly equivariant. Further unindexed equivalent results remain possible.

value.rationale: The natural color-relabeling and position-relabeling symmetries are both intrinsic to graph-coloring manifolds; their simultaneous quotient is the unlabelled-color moduli problem. The complete uniform one-dimensional character classification detects nontrivial target-sign modules not encoded by the classical Stiefel Betti numbers and proves a parity-dependent rational-homology dichotomy of the quotient by both large natural groups. The fixed top-cell and color-boundary projection give structural reasons, not isolated low-order computations. The statement neither asserts a stronger dihedral-equivariant homeomorphism nor relies on routine small-case rank calculation alone.
